decision.reason: No enumerated rendering is both nonfragmentary and ordinary English under the frozen-token policy.

ranking_policy: diagnostic closeness to a complete parse only; never a readability score or certification
scope: closed punctuation/capitalization audit of exactly two fixed tapes; no generation, lexical search, or resegmentation

surface_policy.allowed: punctuation between frozen tokens and sentence-initial capitalization
disallowed: punctuation that hides a forbidden span
hyphenation that invents a compound lexeme

targets.current_rendering: No trace. Note: Spot spoons; snoop; stop. Set one carton.
targets.global_parse_obstruction: With the tokens frozen, a boundary after 'trace' strands 'No trace' as a minor sentence, heading, or elliptical question. Without that boundary, 'note' cannot be the finite predicate of singular 'No trace' (it would be 'notes'); later finite-verb assignments leave agreement or complement debris.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: The determiner phrase 'No trace' has no finite predicate. Treating it as a complete utterance is exactly the fragment reading excluded here.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: [NP no trace] (minor-sentence fragment); [imperative note: [imperative spot [NP spoons]]; [imperative snoop]; [imperative stop]]; [imperative set [NP one carton]].
variants.rendering: No trace. Note: Spot spoons; snoop; stop. Set one carton.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: A semicolon cannot coordinate the bare NP 'No trace' as a clause; supplying 'leave' or 'make' would add lexical material.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: [NP no trace] coordinated with four imperative VPs: note, spot spoons, snoop, stop, and set one carton.
variants.rendering: No trace; note: spot spoons; snoop; stop; set one carton.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: 'No trace?' is an elliptical question (for example, 'Is there no trace?'), not a finite interrogative clause.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: [interrogative NP no trace]? followed by an imperative list.
variants.rendering: No trace? Note: spot spoons; snoop; stop; set one carton.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: The colon turns 'No trace' into a heading, not a clause; 'spot spoons' also requires a coerced compound-object reading.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: [heading NP no trace]: [imperative note [NP spot spoons]]; [imperative snoop]; [imperative stop]; [imperative set [NP one carton]].
variants.rendering: No trace: note spot spoons; snoop; stop; set one carton.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: The singular head 'note' requires 'spots', not 'spot'; reading 'spot' as a noun leaves 'No trace note spot' as an NP fragment.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: Attempted [clause [NP no trace note] [VP spot]]; [clause spoons snoop]; then two imperatives.
variants.rendering: No trace note spot. Spoons snoop; stop; set one carton.

variants.exact_parse_obstruction: The standalone answer particle depends on an unexpressed question, so this rendering still relies on ellipsis.
variants.ordinary_english_parse_attempt: [answer particle no], [imperative trace [NP note spot]]; [clause spoons snoop]; [imperative stop]; [imperative set [NP one carton]].
variants.rendering: No, trace note spot; spoons snoop; stop; set one carton.
